title: Training Dataset — Instruction Pair
description: JSONL format for fine-tuning datasets. Each line is one JSON object matching this schema.
$comment: EVAL-GATE SEMANTICS (Pillar 3 SSOT — see brain/training/evaluator.py, models.py). The fine-tune is gated, before it can serve, on its quality on this dataset, but the gate is built to measure GENERALIZATION, not memorization: (1) HELD-OUT SPLIT — the worker holds out the last ~20% of rows (>=1 row; brain.training.models.split_holdout) and trains only on the rest; the gate scores ONLY the held-out rows, never rows the model trained on. (2) RESPONSE-ONLY LOSS — the score is the cross-entropy on the `response` tokens only; the `prompt`/`system` tokens are masked out (label -100), so it reflects the model's ability to produce the target answer, not to model the operator's prompt text. (3) score = exp(-avg_response_loss) = 1/perplexity, clamped to [0,1]; the gate is an ABSOLUTE floor `score >= eval_score_threshold` (default 0.6, ~perplexity 1.67) → otherwise EvalGateFailed (HTTP 422), adapter not registered, endpoint cannot bind it. (4) RELATIVE SIGNAL — the base (un-adapted) model is also scored on the SAME held-out split and the adapter-minus-base delta is reported (base_score/score_delta) so an operator can see whether the fine-tune actually helped; the gate itself still uses the absolute adapter score.

prompt.description: The instruction or question given to the model.

response.description: The ideal response the model should produce.

metadata.description: Optional arbitrary metadata (source, quality score, etc.)
